daily_summary.es: Apple abre el envío de apps para iOS 27 y su nuevo iPhone Duo plegable mientras OpenAI lanza GPT-6 Astra y reporta un hallazgo matemático usando un modelo aún más avanzado.
daily_summary.en: Apple opens app submissions for iOS 27 and its new foldable iPhone Duo while OpenAI ships GPT-6 Astra and reports a math breakthrough using an even more advanced model.

apple.es: Apple ha lanzado iOS 27, iPadOS 27 y el resto de sus sistemas operativos para 2026, con envíos a la App Store ya abiertos. La release candidate de iOS 27 llega una semana después de la octava beta, con Siri AI en beta (inicialmente solo en inglés), un nuevo slider de opacidad para Liquid Glass y mejoras de rendimiento. Apple también presentó el iPhone Duo, su primer plegable, con doble pantalla OLED a 120Hz y chip A20 Pro de 2nm, y ya publicó recursos para que los desarrolladores adapten sus apps antes del lanzamiento en octubre.
apple.en: Apple has released iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and the rest of its 2026 operating systems, with App Store submissions now open. The iOS 27 release candidate arrives a week after the eighth beta, with Siri AI in beta (initially English-only), a new Liquid Glass opacity slider, and performance improvements. Apple also unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable, with dual 120Hz OLED screens and a 2nm A20 Pro chip, and has already published developer resources ahead of the October launch.

ai_software.es: OpenAI lanzó GPT-6 Astra, su modelo más capaz para negocios, y reportó que un modelo de próxima generación aún no publicado resolvió el problema del milenio de Navier-Stokes en 88 horas usando unos 10,000 agentes, aunque no se han compartido detalles verificables del teorema o la prueba. Por separado, Tibo Sottiaux de OpenAI explicó por qué Codex se construyó en Rust y como código abierto, priorizando rendimiento a escala y compatibilidad con modelos de terceros. Suno lanzó su modelo de música v6 con apoyo de la industria discográfica, y persisten dudas sobre cómo el código generado por IA está cambiando la revisión de código.
ai_software.en: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, its most capable model for business, and reported that an unreleased next-generation model solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem in 88 hours using roughly 10,000 agents, though no verifiable theorem or proof details have been shared. Separately, OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux explained why Codex was built in Rust and as open source, prioritizing performance at scale and compatibility with third-party models. Suno released its v6 music model with record industry support, and questions remain about how AI-generated code is reshaping code review.

ai_general.es: Chris Lehane sostiene que capacidades de IA más fuertes exigen mayor evidencia de seguridad y estándares compartidos mientras la ventana de política pública siga abierta. Mientras tanto, China está regulando a los llamados 'novios de IA', chatbots de compañía, y persiste el debate sobre cuándo el impacto de la IA será tangible para la persona promedio, dado que sus beneficios siguen siendo indirectos.
ai_general.en: Chris Lehane argues that stronger AI capabilities demand stronger safety evidence and shared standards while the public policy window remains open. Meanwhile, China is regulating so-called 'AI boyfriend' companion chatbots, and debate continues over when AI's impact will become tangible for the average person, given that its benefits remain largely indirect.

tech.es: Cloudflare desplegó Automatic Key Exchange, que detecta qué algoritmos de intercambio de claves soportan los orígenes de sus clientes y prioriza conexiones post-cuánticas cuando es posible, cubriendo miles de millones de conexiones diarias. Vercel ahora permite Password Protection por proyecto individual en planes Pro por $20/mes, frente al anterior add-on de equipo de $150/mes. Además, iOS 27 llegará el 14 de septiembre con Siri AI, y un análisis plantea que la industria tiene un año para reforzar la seguridad ante modelos como GLM 5.3-flash, capaces de tareas ofensivas de ciberseguridad.
tech.en: Cloudflare rolled out Automatic Key Exchange, which detects which key agreement algorithms customer origins support and prioritizes post-quantum connections where possible, covering billions of daily connections. Vercel now lets Pro teams enable Password Protection per individual project for $20/month, versus the previous $150/month team-wide add-on. Additionally, iOS 27 launches September 14th with Siri AI, and an analysis argues the industry has one year to shore up security against models like GLM 5.3-flash, which are capable of offensive cybersecurity tasks.

title.es: Apple presenta el iPhone Duo, su primer plegable
title.en: Apple unveils the iPhone Duo, its first foldable

body.es: Apple presentó el iPhone Duo, su primer smartphone plegable, con pantalla exterior OLED de 5.4 pulgadas y una interior de 7.6 pulgadas, ambas a 120Hz. El dispositivo usa el chip A20 Pro, fabricado en un proceso de 2 nanómetros y descrito por Apple como más potente y eficiente que sus antecesores. El precio de entrada es de 2,339 euros para la versión de 256GB, un salto significativo respecto a un iPhone convencional.
body.en: Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone, featuring a 5.4-inch external OLED screen and a 7.6-inch internal OLED screen, both at 120Hz. The device uses the A20 Pro chip, built on a 2-nanometer process and described by Apple as more powerful and efficient than its predecessors. Starting price is 2,339 euros for the 256GB version, a significant jump over a conventional iPhone.

evidence.claim: Apple has launched its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo.
The iPhone Duo features a dual-screen design with an external OLED screen of 5.4 inches and an internal OLED screen of 7.6 inches, both with a 120 Hz refresh rate.
The iPhone Duo is powered by the Apple A20 Pro chip, which is more powerful and efficient than its predecessors.
The iPhone Duo is priced starting from 2,339 euros.

title.es: Apple lanza la release candidate de iOS 27 y iPadOS 27
title.en: Apple seeds iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 release candidates

body.es: Apple liberó las versiones release candidate de iOS 27 y iPadOS 27 para pruebas finales, una semana después de la octava beta. La actualización incluye Siri AI, un chatbot que combina conocimiento general con datos personales de apps como Mensajes y Mail, además de mejoras de rendimiento notables incluso en iPhones antiguos. También se refinó el aspecto de Liquid Glass con un nuevo slider de transparencia.
body.en: Apple released the release candidate versions of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 for final testing, a week after the eighth beta. The update includes Siri AI, a chatbot combining general knowledge with personal data from apps like Messages and Mail, plus notable performance improvements even on older iPhones. Liquid Glass's look was also refined with a new transparency slider.

evidence.claim: Apple has seeded release candidate versions of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 for final testing.
Siri AI is a chatbot similar to ChatGPT, incorporating general world knowledge and personal data from apps.
Apple has improved the performance of iOS, making everything feel faster on older iPhones.

title.es: OpenAI lanza GPT-6 Astra, su modelo más capaz para negocios
title.en: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, its most capable model for business

body.es: OpenAI presentó GPT-6 Astra, descrito por la compañía como su modelo más capaz para uso empresarial, con razonamiento avanzado, uso de computadora y mejor juicio en escritura y diseño. Usuarios tempranos como Peter Yang reportan que destaca en modelado 3D, juegos y pensamiento estratégico, pero a veces describe cómo haría una tarea en lugar de ejecutarla, y no sigue de forma confiable instrucciones personalizadas.
body.en: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra, described by the company as its most capable model for business use, with advanced reasoning, computer use, and stronger writing and design judgment. Early users like Peter Yang report it excels at 3D modeling, games, and strategic thinking, but sometimes describes how it would do a task instead of executing it, and doesn't reliably follow custom instructions.

evidence.claim: GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI’s most capable model for business.

title.es: OpenAI reporta un hallazgo sobre Navier-Stokes con un modelo aún no lanzado
title.en: OpenAI reports a Navier-Stokes finding using an unreleased model

body.es: OpenAI afirmó haber producido una solución al problema del milenio Navier-Stokes en 88 horas, usando un modelo de próxima generación significativamente más capaz que GPT-6 Astra, con un grupo de agentes entrenados durante aproximadamente un año mediante aprendizaje por refuerzo multiagente. Sin embargo, no se ha compartido el enunciado exacto del teorema, un preprint, verificación formal ni comentarios de árbitros independientes, por lo que la afirmación permanece sin confirmar externamente.
body.en: OpenAI claimed to have produced a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem in 88 hours, using a next-generation model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra, with a group of agents trained for about a year via multi-agent reinforcement learning. However, no exact theorem statement, preprint, formal verification, or independent referee commentary has been shared, so the claim remains externally unconfirmed.

evidence.claim: OpenAI reported a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem in 88 hours using a next-generation model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra.
The solution was produced using multi-agent reinforcement learning over the course of about a year.
The exact theorem statement and proof scope are not supplied in the tweet set.
The result was publicly discussed as a Navier–Stokes solution/proof claim.

title.es: Cómo se construyó Codex: Rust, código abierto y compatibilidad con otros modelos
title.en: How Codex was built: Rust, open source, and compatibility with other models

body.es: Tibo Sottiaux, del equipo de Codex en OpenAI, explicó que la herramienta se escribió en Rust priorizando rendimiento y escala para correr en millones de máquinas en la nube, pese a que los modelos de IA eran entonces más fuertes en Python o TypeScript. Codex es de código abierto y funciona con modelos de cualquier proveedor, no solo de OpenAI, lo que Sottiaux ve como una apuesta por dejar que los usuarios elijan el mejor modelo, aunque reconoce que la apertura también facilita que otras herramientas copien su trabajo antes de que se lance.
body.en: OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux explained that Codex was written in Rust, prioritizing performance and scale to run on millions of cloud machines, even though AI models were then stronger at Python or TypeScript. Codex is open source and works with models from any provider, not just OpenAI's, a bet Sottiaux says reflects letting users choose the best model, though he acknowledges openness also makes it easier for other tools to copy its work before release.

evidence.claim: Codex is built using Rust, even though the AI models were much better at writing Python and TypeScript at the time.
Codex is open source, which has upsides and downsides.
Codex supports working with other AI models, not just OpenAI’s.
Maintaining and re-architecting code is becoming very cheap with agents, especially time-wise.
Correctness checks and security reviews will be automated with AI.

title.es: ¿Cuándo sentirá la persona promedio el impacto de la IA?
title.en: When will the average person feel AI's impact?

body.es: Un análisis argumenta que la vida diaria de la persona promedio probablemente cambiará poco en los próximos años porque los beneficios de la IA son demasiado indirectos para notarse, aunque para el trabajo de conocimiento —cerca de la mitad de la economía estadounidense— la IA ya se compara con la electricidad en importancia. El texto advierte que esta desconexión entre impacto real y percepción alimenta un backlash político contra la industria de IA.
body.en: An analysis argues that the average person's daily life will likely change little in the coming years because AI's benefits are too indirect to notice, even though for knowledge work—roughly half of the U.S. economy—AI is already comparable to electricity in importance. The piece warns that this gap between real impact and perception fuels political backlash against the AI industry.

evidence.claim: The average person's daily life will likely remain similar in 50 years due to the indirect nature of AI benefits.
AI is primarily a tool to serve the elite, with knowledge work being significantly impacted.
The AI industry faces political backlash due to the perception of AI as a negative and unsafe technology.
The positive impacts of AI early in its evolution are too indirect for the average person to notice.

title.es: Un modelo abierto y potente en ciberseguridad plantea una carrera de un año para asegurar sistemas
title.en: A powerful open cybersecurity model raises a one-year race to secure systems

body.es: El modelo abierto GLM 5.3-flash, que cualquiera puede descargar y modificar, anota 84.5% en CyberGym y 54.4% en ExploitBench, benchmarks de capacidades ofensivas de ciberseguridad. El análisis argumenta que la industria tiene aproximadamente un año para reforzar sistemas críticos antes de que estas capacidades se generalicen, aunque reconoce que muchos sistemas críticos requieren acceso físico o despliegues escalonados que retrasan la aplicación de parches. Iniciativas como Project Glasswing y Daybreak buscan usar LLMs para corregir fallos de seguridad a escala.
body.en: The open model GLM 5.3-flash, downloadable and modifiable by anyone, scores 84.5% on CyberGym and 54.4% on ExploitBench, benchmarks for offensive cybersecurity capability. The analysis argues the industry has roughly a year to harden critical systems before these capabilities become widespread, though it acknowledges many critical systems require physical access or staged rollouts that delay patching. Initiatives like Project Glasswing and Daybreak aim to use LLMs to fix security issues at scale.

evidence.claim: GLM 5.3-flash can be downloaded and modified by anyone in the world.
The GLM 5.3-flash model scores 84.5% on CyberGym and 54.4% on ExploitBench.
Unified memory in the M5 Mac Studio allows running GLM 5.3-flash with around 45 tokens/second.
Project Glasswing and Daybreak are initiatives to use LLMs to fix security issues across the tech industry.
Critical systems often require physical access or carefully planned staged rollouts to avoid downtime, both of which delay deploying patches.

title.es: Cloudflare despliega intercambio de claves post-cuántico automático
title.en: Cloudflare rolls out automatic post-quantum key exchange

text.es: Cloudflare lanzó Automatic Key Exchange, que detecta qué algoritmos de intercambio de claves soportan los orígenes de sus clientes con TLS 1.3 y prioriza conexiones post-cuánticas cuando están disponibles, aplicándose a miles de millones de conexiones diarias.
text.en: Cloudflare launched Automatic Key Exchange, which detects which key agreement algorithms TLS 1.3-capable customer origins support and prioritizes post-quantum connections when available, applying to billions of daily connections.

evidence.claim: Cloudflare's Automatic Key Exchange probes TLS 1.3-capable customer origins to learn which key agreement algorithms they support.
Cloudflare leads with the most secure algorithm when connecting to the origin.
Cloudflare prefers post-quantum connections when the origin supports it.

title.es: Vercel abarata la protección por contraseña por proyecto
title.en: Vercel cuts the price of per-project password protection

text.es: Los equipos Pro de Vercel ahora pueden activar Password Protection por proyecto individual a $20 al mes, en lugar del anterior add-on de equipo completo por $150 mensuales que cubría todos los proyectos.
text.en: Vercel Pro teams can now enable Password Protection for individual projects at $20 per month, replacing the previous $150-per-month team-wide add-on that covered every project.

evidence.claim: Pro teams can now enable Password Protection for individual projects at $20 per project per month.
Previously, Password Protection was available only through a $150-per-month team-level add-on that covered every project.

title.es: China regula a los chatbots 'novios de IA'

text.es: Los reguladores chinos están apuntando a chatbots de compañía conocidos como 'novios de IA', según reportes, aunque los detalles específicos de la nueva normativa no se han precisado.
text.en: Chinese regulators are targeting AI companion chatbots known as 'AI boyfriends,' according to reports, though the specific details of the new rules have not been specified.

evidence.claim: China's regulators are targeting AI companions known as 'AI boyfriends'.

title.es: Suno lanza su modelo de música v6 con apoyo de la industria discográfica
title.en: Suno releases its v6 music model with record industry support

text.es: Suno lanzó v6, su primer modelo de música con respaldo de la industria discográfica, capaz de crear pistas a partir de imágenes, video u otro audio, y de editar elementos individuales como una línea de guitarra o una letra mediante lenguaje natural en un chat, sin regenerar toda la pista.
text.en: Suno released v6, its first music model made with record industry support, able to create tracks from images, video, or other audio, and to edit individual elements like a guitar line or a lyric using plain language in a chat, without regenerating the entire track.

evidence.claim: Suno's v6 AI music model is its first made with support from the record industry.
Suno's v6 model can create tracks based on images, video, or other audio.
Suno's v6 model can edit parts of a song using plain language within a chat.

trending_repos.name: mlx-serve
trending_repos.description: Native LLM inference server for Apple Silicon. OpenAI + Anthropic API compatible. No Python. Includes MLX Core macOS app with chat, agent mode, and tool calling.

why_it_matters.es: Servidor de inferencia nativo en Zig para Apple Silicon, compatible con las APIs de OpenAI y Anthropic, que ejecuta modelos MLX y GGUF localmente sin Python ni nube; útil para desarrolladores Swift/iOS que quieren correr LLMs on-device.
why_it_matters.en: A native Zig inference server for Apple Silicon, compatible with OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, running MLX and GGUF models locally without Python or the cloud; useful for Swift/iOS developers wanting to run LLMs on-device.

trending_repos.name: vllm
trending_repos.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs

why_it_matters.es: Motor de inferencia y servicio de LLMs de alto rendimiento con más de 91,000 estrellas, que soporta 200+ arquitecturas de modelos y múltiples backends de hardware, incluyendo Apple Silicon; una pieza de infraestructura clave para quien despliega modelos a escala.
why_it_matters.en: A high-throughput LLM inference and serving engine with over 91,000 stars, supporting 200+ model architectures and multiple hardware backends including Apple Silicon; a key infrastructure piece for anyone deploying models at scale.

trending_repos.name: agent-me
trending_repos.description: Distill your knowledge, memories, and decisions into an open-source, inspectable AI Agent Twin.

why_it_matters.es: Arquitectura de código abierto para construir un 'gemelo digital' de IA a partir de conocimiento y decisiones personales, con memoria revisable, recuperación y verificación en lugar de solo un chatbot que recuerda hechos; interesante para quienes exploran agentes personales con trazabilidad.
why_it_matters.en: An open-source architecture for building a personal AI 'twin' from knowledge and decisions, with reviewable memory, retrieval, and verification rather than just a fact-recalling chatbot; interesting for those exploring personal agents with traceability.

why_it_matters.es: Gateway open source que conecta líneas telefónicas SIP con agentes de IA autoalojados, capaz de transferir llamadas, tomar mensajes y usar herramientas HTTP, además de manejar el mismo agente en chat web, SMS y otras 24 plataformas; útil para quienes buscan alternativas autoalojadas a asistentes telefónicos comerciales.
why_it_matters.en: An open-source gateway connecting SIP phone lines to self-hosted AI agents, able to transfer calls, take messages, and invoke HTTP tools, while handling the same agent across web chat, SMS, and 24 other platforms; useful for those seeking self-hosted alternatives to commercial phone assistants.

developer_signals.author: mattpocockuk
developer_signals.original_text:
Alper is right, setting expectations on software quality early is really key

I.e. explicitly calling what you're building a "prototype" can give you a much nicer experience

Whereas if the agent detects it's a finance/medical application you're in for a long grilling https://t.co/pWFJM6vKlp

text.es: Matt Pocock destaca un consejo de Alper Ortac: decirle explícitamente a un agente de IA que un proyecto es un 'prototipo' y que no se debe sobre-diseñar produce sesiones de decisión más rápidas y agradables, evitando que el agente trate cualquier tarea como si fuera una aplicación financiera o médica crítica.
text.en: Matt Pocock highlights a tip from Alper Ortac: explicitly telling an AI agent that a project is a 'prototype' and shouldn't be over-engineered leads to faster, more pleasant decision-making sessions, preventing the agent from treating any task as if it were a critical finance or medical application.

developer_signals.author: petergyang
developer_signals.original_text:
After using GPT-6 Astra as my default model since launch, I’ve found it both incredible and frustrating to work with.

It’s incredible at building 3D games and models, high-level thinking and strategy, and computer and browser use.

But two things keep it from becoming my daily driver:

1. When I ask it to do something, it sometimes tells me how it would do it instead of just getting it done.

2. It doesn’t reliably follow the instructions in my AI skills.

The second issue is especially problematic because it keeps happening even after I cleaned up my skills. If anyone has found a solution, I’m all ears.

For now, I’ll stick with Sol for most execution tasks and use Astra for harder tasks or to get a second opinion.

I wrote more about my impressions of Astra in my new post: https://t.co/mcF7mGuVhL

text.es: Peter Yang comparte impresiones prácticas tras usar GPT-6 Astra como modelo por defecto: es excelente construyendo modelos 3D y juegos con Blender y Godot, y para pensamiento estratégico de alto nivel, pero a veces describe cómo haría una tarea en lugar de ejecutarla y no sigue de forma confiable las instrucciones guardadas en sus 'skills' de IA.
text.en: Peter Yang shares practical impressions after using GPT-6 Astra as his default model: it's excellent at building 3D models and games with Blender and Godot, and at high-level strategic thinking, but it sometimes describes how it would do a task instead of executing it and doesn't reliably follow instructions saved in his AI skills.

developer_signals.author: mattpocockuk
developer_signals.original_text:
I've been trying to use AI for knowledge work (course planning). Here's what seems to work so far:

1. Give each 'deliverable' a Karpathy-style LLM-wiki

(for me, a deliverable is a course, or a talk. A sizeable piece of work, more than 1 day's labour)

2. Split the deliverable into 'sections' that can be worked on in independent threads during the day shift

(more than one thread meads you can parallelize work in different agent threads, all reading from/writing to the wiki for shared state)

3. My input is in the form of braindumps - huge chunks of dictated text the model integrates into its wiki

(it gives me HTML reports, I react to the reports via dictation)

4. Write a 'linting' skill you can run on the entire deliverable during the night shift

(be generous, use a ton of subagents, look for every possible weakness)

This lets me speak the thing I want into existence, with the model capturing everything I say and slowly bringing the thing (course, talk, video) to life.

Work in progress, but I like it.

text.es: Matt Pocock detalla un flujo de trabajo para usar IA en trabajo de conocimiento (planificación de cursos): crear un 'wiki' estilo Karpathy por entregable, dividirlo en secciones trabajables en hilos paralelos, alimentar el modelo con volcados de voz dictados, y correr una skill de 'linting' nocturna con muchos subagentes para detectar debilidades.
text.en: Matt Pocock details a workflow for using AI in knowledge work (course planning): create a Karpathy-style wiki per deliverable, split it into sections that can be worked on in parallel threads, feed the model dictated voice brain-dumps, and run a nightly 'linting' skill with many subagents to find weaknesses.
